NexaWorks | Fictional classroom proposal
1 / 3
FICTIONAL SUPPLIER PROPOSAL · CLASSROOM USE
NexaWorks
Balanced value. Measurable delivery. Accountable support.
01 / Executive summary
Response to the same fictional procurement request: implement a customer-service platform for 250 agents,
integrate CRM and ERP, migrate two million records, and provide secure operations and support for three years.
The buyer seeks clear delivery, commercial and service commitments. All organizations, projects, assurance
documents and references in this proposal are invented.
Understanding the requirement
The buyer needs a single view of service requests, reliable exchange with sales and finance systems, measurable
migration acceptance and auditable access to customer information. The proposed scope and its limitations are
set out below.
Proposed solution
The platform integrates CRM and ERP through versioned REST adapters with idempotent retries and a monitored
dead-letter queue. A containerized service tier supports 500 concurrent agents; staging load tests are included at
1.5 times that volume. An adapter catalogue records field mappings and transformation owners. Data is
partitioned by business unit, with an operational dashboard for failed messages. Offline mobile use is outside the
base scope.
Submitted: 2026-10-19 | Procurement reference: TRAINING-RFP-026

NexaWorks | Fictional classroom proposal
2 / 3
02 / Delivery & commercials
Implementation and milestones
The 12-week plan includes signed stage gates at weeks 2, 6, 9 and 12, with named owners, rollback rehearsal
and a two-week contingency. A RACI assigns the delivery lead, architect, two integration engineers, two
developers, QA engineer and buyer product owner. Gates cover design approval, tested integrations, migration
reconciliation and business acceptance. Acceptance requires 99.5% reconciliation, zero open critical defects and
95% user-test completion. Two migration rehearsals, role-specific training and a four-week hypercare period are
included.
Commercial offer
Three-year total cost is USD 288,000, including integration, training, hosting and four weeks of hypercare.

Assumptions and exclusions
Includes 250 agents, CRM and ERP adapters, and two million migrated records. Annual subscription covers
hosting and support. Prices are fixed for three years; future increases are capped at 5%. Bespoke mobile
development and source-system remediation are excluded. Change requests require an agreed estimate and
written buyer approval.

NexaWorks | Fictional classroom proposal
3 / 3
03 / Assurance & service
Security and compliance
Security includes SAML SSO, MFA for administrators, encryption at rest and in transit, and immutable audit logs
retained for 180 days. The fictional assurance pack NW-2026 lists a penetration-test remediation summary; a full
report is available under NDA in this training scenario. A regional hosting commitment, DPA, 24-hour breach
notice and 30-day deletion process are proposed. Quarterly restoration exercises target RPO 4 hours and RTO 8
hours. No formal ISO certificate is supplied.
Support, experience and references
A dedicated service manager provides 24/7 critical support, a 15-minute response target and a four-hour
workaround target. Seven comparable fictional projects include Oak Logistics (280 agents) and Meadow Services
(240 agents), with reference calls offered during due diligence. Monthly reviews report uptime, backlog and
incident trends. Named backup staff cover holidays, and a knowledge-transfer package is handed over before
hypercare ends. Service credits apply to missed response targets.
Risks and buyer dependencies
Buyer access to source systems, nominated subject-matter experts and timely test decisions are required. Claims
in this proposal require verification before award. Full independent assurance documents require due diligence.
Offline mobile functionality is excluded.
Evidence limitations
This fictional proposal is not an independently verified audit or a real commercial offer. Supporting reference calls,
assurance documents and contract terms are to be reviewed during due diligence. No real confidential supplier
information is included.

Apex Systems | Fictional classroom proposal
1 / 3
FICTIONAL SUPPLIER PROPOSAL · CLASSROOM USE
Apex Systems
Enterprise architecture. Strong controls. Premium investment.
01 / Executive summary
Response to the same fictional procurement request: implement a customer-service platform for 250 agents,
integrate CRM and ERP, migrate two million records, and provide secure operations and support for three years.
The buyer seeks clear delivery, commercial and service commitments. All organizations, projects, assurance
documents and references in this proposal are invented.
Understanding the requirement
The buyer needs a single view of service requests, reliable exchange with sales and finance systems, measurable
migration acceptance and auditable access to customer information. The proposed scope and its limitations are
set out below.
Proposed solution
The solution uses a modular API gateway, event-driven services and an offline retry queue for CRM and ERP
integrations. Two connector prototypes will be demonstrated before build approval. PostgreSQL provides tenant
isolation; Redis caches read-heavy views. Load tests target 1,000 concurrent agents and a 95th-percentile
response below 500 ms. The design includes versioned REST APIs and a reconciliation dashboard for failed
transactions.
Submitted: 2026-10-20 | Procurement reference: TRAINING-RFP-026

Apex Systems | Fictional classroom proposal
2 / 3
02 / Delivery & commercials
Implementation and milestones
Delivery takes 16 weeks: discovery in weeks 1-3, build in weeks 4-10, migration in weeks 11-13 and acceptance in
weeks 14-16. A delivery manager, two integration engineers, three application developers and a QA lead form the
core team. The buyer supplies a product owner and test users. Acceptance requires 98% migration accuracy and
closure of critical defects. A two-week contingency sits within the final phase; dedicated training capacity is not
priced separately.
Commercial offer
Three-year total cost is USD 420,000, excluding taxes and buyer-side network upgrades.

Apex Systems | Fictional classroom proposal
3 / 3
03 / Assurance & service
Security and compliance
Controls include SAML SSO, role-based access, AES-256 storage encryption, TLS 1.3 transport and 365-day
audit logs. A fictional independent control assessment AS-26-14 lists quarterly access reviews and annual
penetration testing. This is a training claim, not a real certification. Recovery objectives are RPO 1 hour and RTO
4 hours, tested every six months. Data stays in the agreed region; a signed DPA and deletion certificate are
proposed before production.
Support, experience and references
Support is available 24/7 for critical incidents, with a 30-minute response target and a named service manager.
Nine comparable fictional projects were delivered in five years. Fictional references: Maple Freight (320 agents)
and Cedar Utilities (210 agents). Reference contact details are intentionally omitted. The support SLA promises a
response, not a guaranteed fix time. Monthly service reviews and quarterly resilience tests are included.
Risks and buyer dependencies
Buyer access to source systems, nominated subject-matter experts and timely test decisions are required. Claims
in this proposal require verification before award. Highest three-year price in this cohort. Training capacity and
resolution SLA need clarification.
Evidence limitations
This fictional proposal is not an independently verified audit or a real commercial offer. Supporting reference calls,
assurance documents and contract terms are to be reviewed during due diligence. No real confidential supplier
information is included.

FICTIONAL SUPPLIER PROPOSAL · CLASSROOM USE
Orbit Digital
Established delivery history. Flexible integration scope.
01 / Executive summary
Response to the same fictional procurement request: implement a customer-service platform for 250 agents,
integrate CRM and ERP, migrate two million records, and provide secure operations and support for three years.
The buyer seeks clear delivery, commercial and service commitments. All organizations, projects, assurance
documents and references in this proposal are invented.
Understanding the requirement
The buyer needs a single view of service requests, reliable exchange with sales and finance systems, measurable
migration acceptance and auditable access to customer information. The proposed scope and its limitations are
set out below.
Proposed solution
The proposal offers a configurable customer-service platform; CRM and ERP integration methods will be agreed
during discovery. The platform supports queue management, dashboards and a searchable knowledge base. The
architecture diagram is described but not supplied. The proposal does not commit to API protocols, message retry
semantics, migration mappings or concurrency targets. Orbit expects its integration partner to confirm feasibility
after a paid discovery workshop.
Submitted: 2026-10-17 | Procurement reference: TRAINING-RFP-026

Orbit Digital | Fictional classroom proposal
2 / 3
02 / Delivery & commercials
Implementation and milestones
Delivery is planned over 14 weeks with discovery, configuration, migration, acceptance testing and a two-week
hypercare period. A senior programme manager, solution consultant, two configuration specialists and one tester
are allocated. Integration engineers are subject to discovery outcomes. Milestones occur at weeks 3, 7, 11 and 14;
buyer sign-off is required at each. Acceptance criteria are to be negotiated. A risk register is reviewed weekly but
schedule contingency is not quantified.
Commercial offer
The estimated three-year total is USD 312,000; custom integration changes are charged at USD 1,200 per
consultant day.

Orbit Digital | Fictional classroom proposal
3 / 3
03 / Assurance & service
Security and compliance
The service supports SSO, encrypted storage, quarterly access reviews and a 90-day audit trail. Orbit describes
an annual external assessment, but no report identifier or certification is included. Backups are retained for 30
days and restoration is tested annually. RTO is one business day; RPO is 24 hours. A standard DPA is offered,
with regional storage location to be agreed. Subprocessor details are available on request.
Support, experience and references
Orbit reports 18 comparable fictional deployments and offers 24/7 critical response within 30 minutes, with named
escalation owners. Three fictional references are offered: Birch Manufacturing (450 agents), Elm Transport (310
agents) and Willow Care (290 agents). Each reference description states implementation dates and scope.
Quarterly training, monthly reviews and a dedicated account lead are included. A four-hour workaround objective
is stated for critical incidents.
Risks and buyer dependencies
Buyer access to source systems, nominated subject-matter experts and timely test decisions are required. Claims
in this proposal require verification before award. Integration architecture and effort are unresolved. Commercial
total may rise with discovery-driven changes. Security assurance documents and data region need confirmation.
Evidence limitations
This fictional proposal is not an independently verified audit or a real commercial offer. Supporting reference calls,
assurance documents and contract terms are to be reviewed during due diligence. No real confidential supplier
information is included.

BrightPath Tech | Fictional classroom proposal
1 / 3
FICTIONAL SUPPLIER PROPOSAL · CLASSROOM USE
BrightPath Tech
Lean scope. Fast launch. Lowest initial commitment.
01 / Executive summary
Response to the same fictional procurement request: implement a customer-service platform for 250 agents,
integrate CRM and ERP, migrate two million records, and provide secure operations and support for three years.
The buyer seeks clear delivery, commercial and service commitments. All organizations, projects, assurance
documents and references in this proposal are invented.
Understanding the requirement
The buyer needs a single view of service requests, reliable exchange with sales and finance systems, measurable
migration acceptance and auditable access to customer information. The proposed scope and its limitations are
set out below.
Proposed solution
A hosted web application will provide ticket queues, email ingestion and a standard CRM connector; ERP
integration uses a nightly CSV export. The platform targets 150 concurrent users at launch. The proposal does not
include a load-test report or offline processing design. A single application instance serves the pilot. The buyer
must supply a clean ERP export format, and changes to its format are billable. A public API is planned but not
committed in the first release.
Submitted: 2026-10-18 | Procurement reference: TRAINING-RFP-026

BrightPath Tech | Fictional classroom proposal
2 / 3
02 / Delivery & commercials
Implementation and milestones
The proposed eight-week schedule allocates one week to discovery, four to configuration, two to testing and one
to launch. The team consists of one project lead, two full-stack developers and a part-time tester. Buyer feedback
is required within one business day. There is no explicit migration reconciliation threshold or contingency
allocation. User training consists of two remote sessions. A slip in buyer decisions moves the go-live date.
Commercial offer
Three-year total cost is USD 156,000, including a fixed implementation fee and three annual subscriptions.

Assumptions and exclusions
Includes 150 named users and one standard connector. Each additional user costs USD 12 per month. Historical
data cleansing is the buyer's responsibility. ERP CSV scripting is included; a real-time ERP connector is excluded.
Travel, taxes and bespoke reporting are excluded. Subscription prices are fixed for the initial three-year term.

BrightPath Tech | Fictional classroom proposal
3 / 3
03 / Assurance & service
Security and compliance
The application uses HTTPS and daily backups; access is controlled by passwords and administrator-managed
user roles. No formal certification, penetration-test report, SSO commitment or audit retention period is supplied.
Backup storage location and restoration time remain to be agreed. BrightPath states that a data processing
agreement can be negotiated after selection. The proposal does not specify breach notification time or regional
hosting boundaries.
Support, experience and references
Support is provided on business days from 09:00 to 17:00, with a one-business-day response target. Two fictional
small-business deployments are described, each with fewer than 50 users. The only fictional reference, Pine
Retail, has not agreed to a reference call. Out-of-hours coverage is a separately priced option and no rate is
provided. Product documentation and recorded training are included.
Risks and buyer dependencies
Buyer access to source systems, nominated subject-matter experts and timely test decisions are required. Claims
in this proposal require verification before award. Security and compliance evidence is limited. Aggressive timeline
has no explicit contingency. Limited experience at the requested scale.
Evidence limitations
This fictional proposal is not an independently verified audit or a real commercial offer. Supporting reference calls,
assurance documents and contract terms are to be reviewed during due diligence. No real confidential supplier
information is included.
